verses.1: And Solomon gave Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, all his treasures. He took Pharaoh’s daughter and brought her to David’s city, so that she could build his house, as well as the house of God and the houses of Jerusalem’s people.
verses.2: Only the people worship in the ruins, because the house was not built for Jehovah until those days.
verses.3: And Solomon loved God to follow the laws of David his father. But only in the moments when he was being sacrificed and burned on the altar.
verses.4: And King Gideon went there to offer sacrifices. It was a very important place; Solomon climbed up onto that altar with his thousand soldiers.
verses.5: In his vision, Jehovah appeared to Solomon in the night. God said, “What shall I give you?”
verses.6: And Solomon said, “You have done a great kindness to your servant David, my father. He went before you in truth, righteousness, and uprightness. You kept this great kindness for him, and gave him a son who will sit on his throne today.”
verses.7: And now, LORD God, you have ruled over your servants under the rule of David, my father. And I am but a little boy, who doesn’t know how long it has been since I was born.
verses.8: And let them serve you within your own people, those whom you have chosen as a people. They are a people who will not be defeated, and whose names will never be forgotten.
verses.9: And You have given to Your servants a heart that can distinguish between good and evil. Who else could judge Your beautiful people?
verses.10: And it was pleasing to Adonai’s eyes, because Solomon asked for this request.
verses.11: And God said to him, “Why did you ask for this? You didn’t ask for many days, nor for wealth, nor for your enemies’ lives. You only asked to be able to hear the judgment.”
verses.12: See, I have done as you commanded. I have given you a wise and intelligent heart, one that is like yours. No one else has ever had such a heart before, and no one else will ever have one like yours after this.
verses.13: And even those whom you did not ask for, I still gave you wealth and honor. None of the kings in all their ages could compare to you in that regard.
verses.14: And if you follow my ways, and keep my laws and commandments, just as your father David did. Then I will bless you during your days.
verses.15: And Solomon built the Temple. Then he went to Jerusalem and stood before the Ark of the Covenant. He made sacrifices and offered offerings for all his servants.
verses.16: Then, two women with beautiful faces came before the king. They stood before him.
verses.17: And the other woman said, “Adonai, I am. And this woman also lives in one house with me.”
verses.18: On the third day after my birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together in that house. There was no one else around us. We were alone in that house.
verses.19: And the son of this woman died that night, as he lay on her.
verses.20: And in the middle of the night, she got up. She took her child from me. Your daughter was still asleep, so she put her child in her arms. And her dead child was also placed in my arms.
verses.21: And in the morning, I went to give birth to my son. But there he was dead. In the morning, I tried to build him up again. But there was no son whom I had given birth to at all.
verses.22: And the other woman said, “Not so. My son is alive, but your son is dead.” She said this not because your son was dead, but because my son was alive. Then she spoke before the king.
verses.23: And the king said, “This is what it means: My son, you are alive; but your son will die. This is what it means: Your son will not live, while my son will die.”
verses.24: And the king said, “Bring me some grapes.” So they brought grapes before the king.
verses.25: And the king said, “Divide the living child between them. Give one half to one person, and give the other half to the other person.”
verses.26: And the woman who had given birth to the baby said to the king, “May your mercy be shown toward her child. Do not kill him; this is what I also say: neither you nor I will be punished.”
verses.27: And the king said, “Give her the living child. Do not kill him; she is his mother.”
verses.28: And all of Israel heard the judgment that the king had made. They saw that it was indeed a judgment given by God, as if He had decided to carry out this judgment.
